story: At 10:17 on this humid, hazy Tuesday in Sumter Oaks, Gary is focused in his garage, running wiring and fitting a speaker mount inside his golf cart while Donna, determined as ever, makes her way down Magnolia Loop to visit him. Hal, equally determined, keeps watch from his house with binoculars, tallying Donna's flamingos and inspecting Gary's cart modifications from a safe distance. Meanwhile Rosa, also determined, works through her pantry and fridge in her kitchen, writing up a grocery list for four.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Run the 12V wiring harness and test-fit the speaker mount inside the cart
Hal (hal binoculars): Scan Magnolia Loop, count Donna's flamingos and check Gary's cart modifications
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Check the pantry and fridge and write the grocery list for four

gary.thought_process: Bench tests are done: speaker works on 12V, LED rope strings light up, wiring plan is sketched. Next step is actually mounting and wiring it all to the cart, which is right here in the garage. L-01 says exterior mods visible from the street need Architectural Review approval, and I skipped that and it's been nagging at me. Wiring the interior and the speaker is fine, but I should be careful and think about what's visible. For now, the productive thing is to get the cart prepped: run the wiring harness and test-fit the speaker mount, keeping everything off the street side until I file the paperwork. Nobody is around, so no one to talk to. This feels good, being useful with my hands again.

parameters.content: Run the 12V wiring harness and test-fit the speaker mount inside the cart

donna.thought_process: I just got back to Magnolia Loop and nobody's in sight. My calendar and bag are sorted, so the practice plan with Gary is set for Saturday at 8. I'm not going to repeat my invitation since I already made it and he showed up. The smart move is to go find him and lock in a practice session before the weekend. His place is right off the loop, so I'll head there with the spare paddle in mind.

parameters.content: Heading over to Gary's to pin down a practice time before Saturday's doubles.

hal.thought_process: I'm home at my porch with the binoculars and notebook right at hand. The notebook already has dated notes on Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos, and Gary admitted himself he's wiring first and filing after. That's a fact I can't unhear. Before I march anything to the committee, a clean visual confirmation from the porch is worth doing. Rules exist so neighbors don't argue, and a documented count beats hearsay. Nobody is nearby, so the binoculars are the right move. I'll count the flamingos and note the cart's modifications as visible from the street. The Buffett speaker business and Gary's garage wiring still sit uneasy with me. I'd rather be accurate than petty.

parameters.content: Scan Magnolia Loop, count Donna's flamingos and check Gary's cart modifications

rosa.thought_process: I'm home at 10:17 AM with the shift schedule, kitchen, and dining table in front of me. I've already blocked off an evening and planned the menu, so the next step in my dinner goal is the groceries. I should check what I actually have in the kitchen for four people and make a shopping list. Nobody's around to talk to, and I've already invited Hal. Gary and Donna still need to hear about it, but I can't reach them from here, so I'll do the practical prep first.

parameters.content: Check the pantry and fridge and write the grocery list for four

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
